title: The Cloud in Your Ice Is Trapped Air
pause_note: Short format v3: 20-30 s, claim first, loop ending

beats: The cloud in your ice is mostly trapped air.
Tap water holds dissolved air. Ice can hold very little.
Your tray freezes from the outside in, pushing the air toward the middle.
The last water to freeze is packed with air, so tiny bubbles form and get locked in.
Freeze it from one side only, and the air is pushed into the last layer.
Cut that off, and the rest of the ice is clear.
That's why a normal cube is cloudy in the middle.
